title: Rezi started as a resume template on Reddit and made $216K in October 2026
dek: A free template, four slow years, then an early bet on AI writing. October 2026 brought in $216,471, read straight from Stripe. That is about 21% less than April 2026 ($275,551), and revenue has dropped every month since. Rezi's MRR (monthly recurring revenue) is $229,097: what all current subscriptions add up to per month, while $216,471 is the money actually collected in October.
pattern: Give it away free, charge for the easy version

cost_to_start.text: Not public. The founder says 2015 to 2018 went on looking for money and paying an agency (an outside company hired to do the work) to build the software, but gives no total.
cost_to_start.label: Claimed

first_revenue.text: A Microsoft Word resume template plus a guide, sold for about $9.69.
first_revenue.label: Claimed

first_customers.short: A resume template shared on Reddit
first_customers.text: Started after a resume template the founder posted on Reddit got used by others. The first product turned users' text into that template.
first_customers.label: Claimed

phases.name: A template on Reddit
phases.story: The founder graduated with low grades but still got interviews at big companies, and put that down to his resume. In May 2015 he posted a resume template built to pass hiring software (called ATS) on Reddit so others could use it. The first thing he sold was that template as a Word file with a short guide.
phases.lesson: Share something genuinely useful for free first; the people who use it tell you what to build.

phases.name: Four slow years
phases.story: The founder moved to South Korea and taught English to pay the bills. A bare-bones tool called Rezi Instant reformatted people's text into the template, with no logins and no database. He spent 2015 to 2018 looking for money and paid an agency to build the real software, which he later called a mistake.

number.v: about 3.5 years of building in Korea
number.label: Claimed

phases.lesson: A tiny version that works today beats a big version you are waiting for someone else to build.

phases.name: Launch as a paid app
phases.story: Rezi launched as a web app with accounts and a paid upgrade in September 2019. Two months later the founder did an AMA (ask me anything) on Reddit, which he calls 'the most authentic channel'. A deal on AppSumo, a site that sells cheap lifetime deals on software, brought in users during the pandemic. StackCommerce, another deals site, brought in revenue.
phases.lesson: Go back to the place your first users came from and talk to them in public.

phases.name: First in line for AI writing
phases.story: When OpenAI released GPT-3, Rezi used it to write resume lines for users, while the team was just two people. By March 2021 the homepage said 'POWERED BY GPT-3' and 'THE FIRST GTP-3 POWERED RESUME BUILDER', typo included.

number.v: "Create Your Resume With Rezi. AI-Powered ATS Resume Builder"
number.label: Wayback

phases.lesson: When a new tool appears, ask what boring part of your product it could do for the user.

phases.name: The ChatGPT wave
phases.story: When ChatGPT made everyone curious about AI, Rezi was already an AI resume builder. The company says it hit $1M a year in recurring revenue in March 2023 and 1 million users in July 2023. In January 2023 the plans were Free, $3 a month and $29 a month.
phases.lesson: Be ready before the wave arrives; you can't build fast enough once it does.

phases.name: Search, not ads
phases.story: The founder says Rezi spent about $15K a month on paid ads for a year without making the money back, then stopped. Growth came from search results instead: Rezi ranks for 'AI Resume Builder'. He also removed the $3 plan, which he says made each customer worth more. But since April 2026 revenue has fallen every month, from $275,551 to $216,471 in October, about 21% less. We couldn't find a public reason.
phases.lesson: If ads don't pay for themselves after a fair test, stop and put that money into something that keeps paying off over time, like search. Then keep checking your numbers, because growth can stall.

fact_checks.claim: The free-plan giveaway brought just under 70,000 signups in one day in October 2023
fact_checks.found: Rezi's own 2023 review mentions 55,376 new users in less than a day in November 2023, without saying why. If it's the same day, the month and the number differ.
fact_checks.label: Sources differ

fact_checks.found: The same page says 15 employees in one place and 11 in another. Rezi's 2023 review says 12. TrustMRR lists 1 founder, which counts founders, not staff.
fact_checks.label: Sources differ

fact_checks.found: TrustMRR's monthly series starts in Dec 2025, so we can't check Aug 2024. Since then every month has been between $216,471 and $275,551.
fact_checks.label: Couldn't verify

fact_checks.found: TrustMRR shows $10,641,968 all-time on Nov 28 2026, and $2,723,056 of that came in Dec 2025 to Oct 2026 alone. That is consistent with $5M+ in March 2025, but no verified number shows the total on that date, so we can't confirm it.
fact_checks.label: Couldn't verify

checklist: Make one template, checklist or guide that solves a problem you just solved for yourself, and post it free in the subreddit where people ask about it.
Count how many people download or ask for it in a week. That is your first proof.
Offer a paid version that does the boring part for them, even if it's just a file and a guide.
Build the smallest tool that works (a form that fills in your template) instead of waiting to build the full app.
Pick one new AI feature and test whether it saves your user five minutes.
Write one helpful page that answers a question people search for, and check in a month whether anyone found it.
